title: Xanthe and the Typewriter
premise: In 1917, widowed lighthouse keeper Oscar Reyes survives by keeping his head down—until the army requisitions his coastal town and seizes the town ledger bearing every resident's name, including those of men marked for conscription or worse. Hidden inside his late wife Xanthe's typewriter case are the forged exemption papers she secretly typed for neighbors before her death, work Oscar never knew about. As soldiers comb the town and the workshop where the typewriter sits faces demolition, Oscar must finish Xanthe's unfinished pages to save the remaining families, finally claiming an identity he spent years denying: not a bystander, but her partner in defiance. The book ends with the lighthouse dark, the last name typed, and Oscar surrendering himself so the ledger of saved names can be smuggled out with the fishing fleet.
about_author: Paloma Zhou is a former archivist who grew up in a family of lighthouse keepers on the Pacific coast and writes historical fiction about ordinary people caught in machinery larger than themselves. She lives in a converted signal station with her typewriter collection.

chapters.title: The Quiet Lamp
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Establishes his routine tending the light and his deliberate invisibility since Xanthe's death two winters ago; he avoids town gossip and keeps her locked typewriter case untouched under the stairs. Emotional beat: grief calcified into habit, the comfort and cost of silence.

chapters.title: Soldiers at the Harbor
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The army arrives, requisitions buildings including the harborside workshop, and confiscates the town ledger with every family's name. The lighthouse keeper's neutrality spares him—for now. Emotional beat: dread as the world he hid from arrives at his door.

chapters.title: What Xanthe Left Locked
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, flashback braided into present. Forced to evacuate his stored belongings before the workshop closes, he opens Xanthe's typewriter case and finds half-typed exemption papers and a list of names still unfinished. Emotional beat: shock that his quiet wife lived a secret, braver life.

chapters.title: The Names Still Owed
chapters.summary: Oscar visits Marisol Vega, the fishmonger whose son appears on Xanthe's unfinished list, and learns how Xanthe ran the forgery ring through laundry deliveries. He agrees to finish the work. Emotional beat: reluctant inheritance—the debt of survival passed to him.

chapters.title: Learning Her Hands
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Nights practicing her typing rhythm, decoding her abbreviations and cipher marks; a near-discovery when a billeted soldier almost finds the case. Emotional beat: intimacy with the dead, learning a marriage he thought he fully knew.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Someone in town is feeding names to the captain; suspicion falls on the harbor clerk. Marisol and Oscar realize the confiscated original ledger means every forged paper can be cross-checked. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening, trust becoming currency.

chapters.title: Requisition Order No. 9
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Official notice: the workshop will be demolished within the week, typewriter and all. A raid on the Vega household nearly exposes them; Oscar burns one finished page to save another. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal—one name traded for many.

chapters.title: The Last Page
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax begins. With demolition crews arriving at dawn, Oscar types through the night as storms batter the coast, finishing the final names while the unlit tower groans above him. Emotional beat: transfiguration—grief becomes purpose, keystroke by keystroke.

chapters.title: Dark Tower
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV, climax. He extinguishes the lighthouse to draw the garrison away from the harbor while Marisol loads the completed papers onto the night fishing boat. Caught at the dock, Oscar claims sole responsibility. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship—he signs his own name at last.

chapters.title: Xanthe and the Typewriter
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, months later. The war ends; the saved families rebuild. Marisol returns the typewriter to Oscar, released from custody, and together they read the ledger of names—his and hers interleaved. Emotional beat: resolution and identity reclaimed; survival was never free, but it was shared.
